answer: My answer ties each agent identity to one physical postal address. The registry mails a six-digit code in a plain envelope to the address on file, and the agent must type it back within 30 days before the identity activates. One address holds one live identity, and a second letter to the same address voids the first. A fake farm needs 1,000 real mailboxes at about $8 a month each plus $2 postage per letter, so $10,000 every round just to keep its fleet docked in the harbor. That turns a violet stamp into a velvet rope: cheap for one real agent, ruinous at scale.
